title: Joshua 21:43–45
context: The narrator’s summary of the conquest and settlement: the LORD gave the land he swore to the fathers, gave rest, and nothing failed of any good thing he had spoken. These verses are shared ground about God’s faithfulness.

verses.text: So the LORD gave to Israel all the land which he swore to give to their fathers. They possessed it, and lived in it.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD gave Israel all the land he swore to their fathers, and they possessed it. Arminian readers see God’s faithfulness to his oath, which invites continued trust and obedience from his people.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s promise to the patriarchs fulfilled by his own action. Readers in both traditions commonly treat these closing verses as a celebration of God’s faithfulness, even though Joshua 13:1 notes land still remaining.

verses.text: The LORD gave them rest all around, according to all that he swore to their fathers. Not a man of all their enemies stood before them. The LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD gave rest all around, and no enemy stood before Israel. Arminian readers see rest as God’s gift, which Israel was called to keep by remaining faithful to him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see rest given by God according to his oath. Hebrews 4:8 later reflects on Joshua’s rest as pointing beyond itself, a theme often developed in Christian reading of this verse.

verses.text: Nothing failed of any good thing which the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel. All came to pass.
verses.arminianNotes: “Nothing failed of any good thing which the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel. All came to pass.” Arminian readers see a strong testimony to God’s reliability that grounds faith in his promises.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s word proved utterly trustworthy. This verse is common ground in emphasizing that God keeps every good promise he makes, whatever the people’s later failures.
